To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the use of complex network theory for the analysis of genetic data can be made feasible by the use of an appropriate iterative feature selection strategy, and that this approach can be successfully applied to the analysis of the genetic information of patients with Obstructive Naphropathy.

the use of an appropriate preprocessing strategy allows to identify a reduced subset of relevant features, that can be used to construct complex networks, whose topology still contains all relevant information about the insurgence of the disease.

we are able to reduce the computational cost of a complex networks approach by a factor of 10, without losing information.

, by using a simple preprocessing strategy, the analysis of genetic data can be performed in a more efficient and reliable way.

the use of feature selection techniques can help in the analysis of large datasets, thus enabling the study of diseases with a genetic origin, for which a large number of relevant features are available.
the proposed feature selection strategy is a powerful tool to reduce the computational cost of complex networks analysis, while preserving its predictive power.
